runs.text: How the shared build-cache disk failed
Every runner read from and wrote to the same shared disk.
When one job saturated that disk, unrelated builds queued behind it.
A full or slow volume failed builds that had nothing else in common.

slide.notes: The old failure mode was shared fate: one disk, every build.

runs.text: What we changed: the cache moved to an object store
Cache entries became objects, each keyed by its own content.
Every build now fetches and writes on its own, with no shared lock.
Capacity grows with use, without resizing a volume.

slide.notes: The change replaced one shared disk with independent object reads and writes.

runs.text: What the move did to build times
One busy build can no longer slow down the rest.
Builds spend less time waiting on the cache, so they finish sooner.
A cache fault now affects a single build rather than all of them.

slide.notes: The effect: no more queuing behind one disk, and shorter waits on the cache.
